title: This crypto paper bot is +32% after 7 days while BTC is +1.6%.. would you copy it or call it noise?
author: GreatBreadfruit8139
selftext:
This crypto bot is +31.9% in 7 days while BTC did +1.6%.. signal or just early luck?

One bot in my public Paper League is starting to look interesting..

PSTE 8H · PSAR 12H

7 days.. +31.9% return  
BTC same period.. +1.6%  
ETH.. -0.88%  
Max DD.. -0.08%  
Trades.. 5

The configuration was frozen from creation.. so there’s no changing the rules after seeing the result.

Obviously 5 trades proves almost nothing.. but this is exactly the stage I find interesting.

Do you copy it into Paper now and watch it forward?.. or wait until 30–50 trades and potentially miss the early part?

[https://app.labnarrative.com/league/pste-8h-psar-12h-2b170599](https://app.labnarrative.com/league/pste-8h-psar-12h-2b170599)

Paper/simulated Spot trading only.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
noise, but the useful kind. five trades with almost no drawdown and a result that size means one or two of those five did nearly all of it, so the first thing to look at isn't the total, it's the same table with the best trade removed. if that's near flat, you have one lucky entry and a frozen config, which is still better than most posts here because the frozen part is the honest part.

copy or wait is a false choice in paper. copying costs you nothing, so copy it, but write the judgement down today, before the next thirty trades: how many trades, what drawdown kills it, what it has to show without the best trade to stay. the mistake isn't watching early, it's deciding the criteria after you've seen the result, which is the same sin as changing the rules, just moved one step downstream. a 7-day window on an 8h and 12h signal is maybe fifteen bars of decisions, so wait for a number of trades, not a number of days.

replies.author: GreatBreadfruit8139
replies.body:
That’s a good way to frame it.. especially the “best trade removed” check.

I agree the mistake isn’t watching early, it’s moving the goalposts after seeing what happened. I’d rather define the survival criteria now.. minimum trades, max acceptable drawdown, and whether the result still looks meaningful without the best trade. And yes, for an 8H/12H setup, trade count is probably a much better clock than days.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: minimum trades gets skipped most. thirty before I call it anything, and the drawdown line as a dollar figure rather than a percent of a balance you picked yourself. then hands off the config until it gets there. you're the one running the frozen bot board, so you have the graveyard to check it against anyway.

replies.author: GreatBreadfruit8139
replies.body: Agreed.. 30 trades before calling it anything, define the drawdown limit in actual dollars, and leave the config completely untouched until then. And yes, comparing it against the failed/retired bots is probably just as important as watching the survivor itself.. the graveyard gives the result context.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the graveyard is the control group. one more thing worth writing down before the 30 trades land: the number that kills it. decide that now, because at trade 25 with a drawdown on the screen you'll find a reason not to.

comments.author: ciaranwalsh96
comments.body:
Disclosure: I own WalletInvestor. One measurement question before interpreting the -0.08% drawdown: does it use total account equity, including open positions, or only the balance after trades close?



Your public page currently shows 5 trades but 2 closed trades (one win, one loss). It would help to label whether the five means orders, entries, or completed round trips. Those are different sample sizes.



For the next report, I'd show the equity curve including open P&L and state how often it's sampled. A position can fall substantially and recover before closing; a closed-trade balance curve won't show that path. If you already include open positions, adding the sampling interval beside the drawdown figure would make the result much easier to assess.

replies.author: GreatBreadfruit8139
replies.body:
Right now the 5 trades means total positions/trade records opened, while the 2 closed trades are completed round trips.  
  
on drawdown: the current calculation is not yet a continuously sampled mark-to-market equity curve. It uses the closed-trade equity history and adds current unrealized P&L, so a position could dip hard intratrade and recover before closing without that full path being captured.

replies.author: ciaranwalsh96
replies.body:
Thanks for spelling that out. I'd put that limitation beside the drawdown number, since adding today's unrealized P&L cannot recover earlier dips. The trade labels could simply be 'positions opened' and 'completed round trips'.



A useful regression test for the new calculation: with no deposits or withdrawals, feed it total-equity snapshots of 10,000, 9,000, then 10,500 at the final exit. Maximum drawdown should remain 10% even though the trade finished profitable.



Store timestamped cash plus the market value of all open positions, with fees reflected, at a stated sampling interval. Mark when that recording starts; unless you can reconstruct the earlier path, don't present the new drawdown series as covering the whole experiment. Even regular snapshots can miss moves between samples.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: I'd call it noise for now, and copying it into paper to watch forward costs nothing, as long as you treat it as an experiment with a pre-set review date. Two completed trades with a 31.9% return suggests big position sizes or one large winner, so I'd look at how much of the gain came from a single trade and how much capital was at risk. The drawdown figure also isn't sampled continuously, as the thread notes, so -0.08% likely understates it. The useful test is the number of independent trades over a few weeks, compared with BTC and with the other bots in the same family. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for checking if the gain lined up with a scheduled news move.

replies.author: GreatBreadfruit8139
replies.body:
Agreed.. “interesting noise” is probably the right label for now 😂

I also want to check how concentrated the +31.9% is.. if one trade did most of the work, that changes the interpretation a lot.

The next useful milestone for me is more independent trades under the same frozen config, compared against BTC/ETH and the other bots in the family.. and yes, checking whether the gains line up with a few macro/news days is worth doing too.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That's the right next step, and writing the number of trades and the review date down before the next batch comes in will keep it clean. Thanks for taking the points on board, I'll look out for the update.

replies.author: GreatBreadfruit8139
replies.body:
That’s a very useful way to test it.. especially the 10k > 9k > 10.5k example. The max DD should still show 10% even though the trade eventually closed profitable.

I agree the fix is proper timestamped total-equity snapshots: cash + marked value of open positions, with fees included.. and the sampling interval needs to be disclosed next to the drawdown.
